limitations_and_boundaries: Assumes sufficiency (no hidden variables that are common causes of at least two observed variables).
Does not provide formal guarantees on the learned structure (uncertainty about whether predicted edges correspond to causal relations).
Experiments limited to synthetic data; no real-world datasets evaluated.
Hyperparameters not optimized; same ℓ1 penalty coefficient used across all graphs, which may not be optimal.
Wall time limit of 36 hours may have constrained performance for larger graphs.
DAGMA's convergence may be affected by choice of s and μ schedule; smaller s requires smaller learning rates.
Only first-order optimizer (ADAM) used; second-order methods not explored.

experiments_or_tasks: Develop DAGMA, a method that resembles the central path for barrier methods, solving a sequence of unconstrained problems regularized by the log-det function.
Evaluate DAGMA against GES, PC, NOTEARS, and GOLEM on linear and nonlinear SEMs with various graph types and noise distributions.
Propose a new acyclicity characterization based on the log-determinant function, leveraging the nilpotency property of DAGs and relating the domain to M-matrices.

methods.name: DAGMA
methods.protocol_description: Algorithm 1: Initialize θ(0) so that W(θ(0)) ∈ Ws (e.g., zero matrix). For t=0,...,T-1, solve θ(t+1) = arg min_θ μ(t)(Q(fθ; X) + β1∥θ∥1) + hs_ldet(W(θ)) starting at θ(t), then set μ(t+1) = αμ(t). Use ADAM optimizer for the unconstrained subproblems. Parameters: μ(0)=1, α=0.1, β1=0.01, s=1, T iterations.
